chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Trumpet, drums, then trombone; self-taught
summary: He tried trumpet and drums before the trombone, which he first played seriously at school in 1926 and took lessons on later.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Is the trombone the first instrument you
I fooled around with trumpet a while. It just got a little too rough for me. And I fooled around with drums a little while but --

Oh, I was just a kid. I was -- I guess I was 15, 14, 15. When I first left Savannah I fooled around with so many instruments. But around Savannah I had picked up a trumpet and fooled around with that a lot, more than I did with trombone. And I didn't own any instrument.

Then I used to fool around -- there was a guy named Freddie Slee had drums, and I used to fool around with his drums. And he was a pretty bad drummer too. He couldn't play good. But he had drums, you know.
Do you remember how old you were when you first started fooling around with the trumpet?

Yeah, I guess I was about 12. Because the first time I really did get around with a trombone where I would fool around with it all day and things like this was when I first went to that school in 1926. I had messed around. I could play a little blues on trombone. I had worked out a little bit of blues but I didn't know too much about it. I didn't know anything about what I was doing.
So, you sort of taught yourself?
Yeah. At first, yeah. I took lessons
